title: California's Governor Race Is So Close We Still Don't Know Who Won!
summary: Have you ever been in a race where you couldn't tell who crossed the finish line first? That's what happened in California's primary election for governor on Tuesday night. With 60 candidates on the ballot, it was a giant contest, and the top two finishers will move on to the final election in November. As of Wednesday, Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton were in the lead, but Democrat Tom Steyer was close behind. Votes are still being counted, so nothing is final yet. Becerra used to be the U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services. He told supporters in Los Angeles that he was the underdog—someone nobody expected to win. 'Here in Hollywood's hometown, we love a good underdog success story,' he said. Hilton is a former Fox News commentator who was born in Britain and became a U.S. citizen five years ago. He said change is 'long overdue' in California, where Democrats have been in charge for 16 years. Steyer, a billionaire, spent over $213 million of his own money on his campaign. He said he'll wait until every ballot is counted. The winner will replace Governor Gavin Newsom, who can't run again. Because California's primary is open to everyone, the two top vote-getters advance even if they're from the same party. So stay tuned—this race isn't over yet!
why_it_matters: This race matters because the governor makes decisions about schools, parks, and safety that affect kids across California and can influence the whole country.

keywords.explanation: A primary election is a vote to choose which candidates will compete in the final election.
A Democrat is a member of one of the two major U.S. political parties, usually favoring more government services.
A Republican is a member of the other major U.S. party, often supporting lower taxes and fewer government rules.
An underdog is someone who is expected to lose a contest.
A commentator is a person who gives opinions on news events, often on TV.
A billionaire is a person with at least one billion dollars.

background_read: California is the most populous state in the U.S., so its governor leads millions of people. Before the final election, a primary election narrows down the many candidates to just two. In this race, Xavier Becerra (who was the U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services) and Steve Hilton (a former Fox News commentator) are leading, but billionaire Tom Steyer is close behind.
Article_Structure: WHO: Democrat Xavier Becerra, Republican Steve Hilton, and Democrat Tom Steyer, along with many other candidates.
WHAT: A primary election for governor of California is too close to call.
WHY: Because votes are still being counted, and the top two will advance to the final election in November.
